The best way to minimize bias is to focus political discussion on the specific proposals, drafts, and bills being debated by legislative bodies.

When discussing specific policy proposals, people can more easily enter an objective discussion of a proposal's relevant merits and flaws, and more easily employ methods for rational decision making such as weighing the pros and cons.

When people are discussing the press releases and public statements of executive branch candidates, it becomes much harder to do so.

This is because the seed of the conversation will often times little more than a superficial and intentionally provocative statement deliberately made for purposes of social engineering.

The problem with attempting to categorize political discussion as liberal, conservative, and independent is that it falsely assumes these labels mean consistent things across different countries, or that these labels mean consistent thing across different time periods in the same country.

Labels such as 'conservative' for instance might refer to radically different policies depending on the political history of the country in which one resides and depending upon how far back in that countries history one wishes to look or romanticize.

In many countries conservatism could actually be referring to communism.

Questions:

Who qualifies as the liberal to represent an entire view? Who qualifies as a conservative? Would it be Sean Hannity versus Alan Combs?

What if I say I don't like the conservative because he's not a "true" conservative?

In a place flooded with independents, can we really divide up the views into neat little categories?

First of all, we all have bias. Let's be up front about our own biases. Also, don't downvote simply because you disagree. Instead, actually comment and start a conversation.

Respect other people. You don't have to respect their opinions or beliefs - but empathize with them. People can be fooled, biased, or mislead - but so can you. Be confident enough in your beliefs that you don't have to call someone else stupid to feel better about your opinion. When you see a political view you disagree with, consider that this is a person who is ultimately capable of anything (like you) and they will benefit from hearing your outlook in a reasonable and respectful way. You won't convince anyone in a day - but the seeds of a wise argument born of facts and solid discourse can bend any man over the course of time and consideration.

Remember: you ARE NOT ALWAYS right. You too have been fooled, biased, and mislead. In your mind, do not immediately jump to /this person is stupid/ or /this person should not be allowed to discuss politics/; instead you should carefully consider their views and how they came to those views - ask how if they do not share. After that, share what you have heard, and then what you know - which are two very different things, the little of the latter may surprise and disarm you.

do not anticipate an /end/ to a friendly debate. Remember when I said that you cannot convince someone in a day? That is a good trait - most of your conversation should end with /to be continued/ and never a final score. this is not a game, an exhibition of intelligence, or an IQ test. This is a friendly debate - an opportunity to learn new views, counter arguments, and to see something you were not capable of seeing before. You are looking for evidence that could lead to your opinion being right OR the opposing position being right. If you only look for evidence that YOU need for YOUR argument to be right, then you are blinding yourself. Be open to being wrong for the rest of your life, for the moment you shut out other possibilities - that is the day your perspective stops growing and your value as an intellect dies. It's very hard to shake free of your own narrow-mindedness - so please be wary of it, as finding the answer that is always right is NOT the goal; you must come to every discourse ready to learn and understand a new answer that you could not before.

Act like a grown-up of a new generation. Be slow to anger, always ready to empathize, and encourage the idea that we always have more to learn - yes, even you.

all you have to do is manually edit the client.dll with any text editor like notepad or notepad++ (yes it works)

Usually the client.dll is located here:

C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\SteamApps\common\dota 2 beta\dota\bin\client.dll

you might want to make backup of it, but you should get new version anyway by just deleting client.dll (I think).

Anyways, once you found your client.dll, open it with notepad and search with ctrl+f hotkey for "-override_vpk" (without the quotes) and

replace it with

"1234567890123" (without the quotes) It doesn't have to be those numbers but the

text has to be same length, then you can just save the file with ctrl+s and

add -override_vpk to your launch parameters and it will work :)
